inline_comments.comment: `radar` was removed from the `required` list and replaced with `venn` instead of being added alongside it. The correct fix is to append `- venn` as a new entry, keeping `- radar`. As written, this is a regression: JSON Schema validation no longer requires a `radar` property to be present in a valid `MermaidConfig` object, silently relaxing the schema contract for existing radar diagram users.

The project rule requires calling `configureSvgSize` *before* setting the `viewBox` attribute, following the pattern established in `pieRenderer.ts`. Here, `viewBox` is set manually at this line while `configureSvgSize` is called at the end of the function (line 109). Although `configureSvgSize` does not itself overwrite `viewBox`, the ordering still violates the established convention and could cause subtle issues if the helper's implementation is ever updated.

Using `as never` to silence a TypeScript error on the call to `vennDiagram` is a broad suppression that hides the underlying type mismatch between D3's `call()` signature and the `@upsetjs/venn.js` chart function. Per project rules, `@ts-ignore` or unsafe casts should not be used to work around incorrect type annotations; the correct fix is to type `vennDiagram` with the appropriate callable signature, or add a narrow cast with a comment explaining why it's safe (e.g., `as Parameters<typeof dummyD3root['call']>[0]`).

The hardcoded fallback `?? 15` does not match the schema-declared default of `8` for `padding`. If `config` is ever `undefined` (e.g., in a test that does not stub `getConfig`), the renderer silently uses a different padding than the schema specifies. Use the schema default (`8`) as the fallback, or — better — ensure `config` is always populated by removing the unnecessary `?.` optional chaining on `db.getConfig` (which is a required method of `DiagramDBBase`).

`config` is inferred as `Required<VennDiagramConfig> | undefined` because of the optional chaining on `db.getConfig?.()` at line 21, yet `renderTextNodes` expects `Required<VennDiagramConfig>` (non-optional). The optional chaining is unnecessary: `getConfig` is a required method on `DiagramDBBase`, so `db.getConfig` is always defined. Remove the `?.`, assign `const config = db.getConfig()`, and let TypeScript infer the non-nullable type. This also fixes the redundant `config?.useDebugLayout` and `config?.padding` guards inside `renderTextNodes`.

Module-level mutable arrays/sets (`subsets`, `textNodes`, `knownSets`, `currentSets`, `indentMode`) leak state across parallel diagram renders. The project rule recommends wrapping all mutable DB state in `ImperativeState` (see `packages/mermaid/src/utils/imperativeState.ts`). Even if the existing `radar` module uses the same pattern, the canonical reference for new diagrams is `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/packet/db.ts`, which uses `ImperativeState`.

`value ?` is a falsy check, so an empty string `''` is treated as absent and returned as-is rather than being passed through `normalizeText`. Per project rules, use a strict `=== undefined` (or `!= null`) check instead:
```ts
const normalizeStyleValue = (value: string | undefined): string | undefined =>
  value !== undefined ? normalizeText(value) : value;
```

`customClear` does not reset `yy.consumeIndentText`. This property is set directly on the `yy` (db) object by the jison lexer when it detects an indented `text` line. If a parse fails mid-stream while `consumeIndentText` is `true`, the subsequent parse call will incorrectly suppress the first `TEXT` token it encounters. Add `this.consumeIndentText = false` (or `(db as any).consumeIndentText = false`) at the end of `customClear` to guarantee a clean state on reset.
The import is named `flowStyles`, which is a copy-paste artifact from the flowchart diagram. This should be `vennStyles` (or simply `styles`) to accurately reflect what the import contains.

`VennChartStyleOptions` lists many properties that are specific to the flowchart diagram and are entirely unused for Venn rendering: `arrowheadColor`, `clusterBkg`, `clusterBorder`, `edgeLabelBackground`, `lineColor`, `mainBkg`, `nodeBorder`. These appear to have been copied wholesale from the flowchart styles. Remove any field not actually consumed in the `getStyles` template, and trim the interface down to only what the Venn diagram needs.

Several `//`-style comments appear inside the CSS template literal (e.g., lines 78–83, the `// background-color:` stub, and `// fill: ${...}` inside `.node .cluster`). `//` is not valid CSS; it is a JavaScript comment syntax. While Stylis may tolerate it in some contexts, it can cause parsing issues in other CSS processors. Either remove these leftover stubs entirely (they appear to be dead code from the flowchart template) or convert them to `/* ... */` CSS block comments.

The metadata `title` is `'Sales Revenue'` but the actual diagram code describes "Three overlapping sets" (A, B, C). This is a copy-paste error from another diagram's example entry. The title should match the diagram content — something like `'Three Overlapping Sets'`.

The `%%{init: { ... }}%%` directive syntax is deprecated in this project and must not be introduced in new code. Use the frontmatter YAML block instead:
```
venn-beta
---
config:
  theme: dark
  themeVariables:
    background: '#0d1117'
---
```
This applies to all three occurrences of `%%{init}%%` in this file.

A `<style>` block with fully commented-out properties (`/*width: 45vw;*/`, `/*padding: 2em;*/`) was committed at the bottom of the file. This is a scratch/debug artifact and should be removed before merging.

Per project rules, a new diagram's config entry in `defaultConfig.ts` must explicitly set `useMaxWidth: true` to match all other diagrams. The current entry only spreads `defaultConfigJson.venn`, which inherits `useMaxWidth` from the schema's `BaseDiagramConfig` default. Add it explicitly for clarity and to guard against future schema-default changes:
```ts
venn: {
  useMaxWidth: true,
  ...defaultConfigJson.venn,
},
```

general_comments.comment: `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/venn/styles.ts` was largely copied from the flowchart diagram's styles and was not cleaned up. Beyond the interface issue noted on `VennChartStyleOptions`, the CSS template itself contains many entirely irrelevant rules: `.node rect/circle/ellipse/polygon/path`, `.arrowheadPath`, `.edgePath .path`, `.flowchart-link`, `.flowchart-label text`, `.flowchartTitleText`, `.edgeLabel`, `.labelBkg`, and several cluster-related rules. None of these selectors are emitted by the Venn renderer. They add dead weight to the stylesheet, risk unintended style collisions, and make it harder to understand what the Venn diagram actually styles. The file should be rewritten from scratch to contain only rules needed for `.venn-circle`, `.venn-intersection`, `.venn-text-node`, `.venn-text-area`, and the diagram title.

The jison grammar (`venn.jison`) allows a non-indented `TEXT identifierList stylesOpt` form where the identifier list is interpreted as the target set names and the text node's `id` is always set to `""` (empty string). This form is undocumented — the docs only show the indented form — and an empty-string `id` could cause silent collisions if multiple non-labeled text nodes are added to the same area. Consider either documenting this non-indented form explicitly (with a note about the empty id) or removing it from the grammar to keep the syntax surface minimal while the diagram is in beta.
